title: Preservation of the Jacobi invariant
statement: Let $z$ and $S$ be bit strings satisfying the following condition: there are bit strings $A,N,s$ with $S=\langle A,\langle N,s\rangle\rangle$, $|A|\le |z|$, $|N|\le |z|$, and $|s|\le 1$, such that if the integer represented by the second projection of $z$ is odd, then the integer represented by $N$ is odd and the product of the sign encoded by $s$ with the Jacobi symbol of the integers represented by $A,N$ equals the Jacobi symbol of the integers represented by the first and second projections of $z$. After one Jacobi step on $S$, the resulting state still satisfies this condition for the same $z$.
hypotheses_covered: Existence of bit strings $A,N,s$ encoding $S$ as a nested pair
If the value of the second projection of $z$ is odd, then the value of $N$ is odd and the signed Jacobi-symbol identity holds
caveat: The statement's invariant is rendered explicitly, but the Jacobi step is defined by a detailed bit-level update whose full case distinction is not expanded here.
